title: Oracle jumps into payments for retailers
summary: Oracle has expanded its services for retailers to include in-store payment acceptance, offering tap-to-pay capabilities for various payment methods like debit, credit, Apple, Google, and Samsung digital wallets. This new feature, which became available in December, will be sold at a fixed fee without long-term contracts or minimum monthly payment volumes. Oracle aims to provide a more stable and cost-effective "payment to processing" solution, integrating it with their existing hardware and cloud-based software for inventory and staff management.

title: Buffett-Backed Taiwan Semiconductor Braces for Chip-Sector Downturn
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) reported record profits for its fourth quarter, exceeding analyst expectations, but also issued a warning about a potential downturn in demand for 2023. This news comes as the company, backed by Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway, indicates higher costs for building facilities in the U.S. compared to Taiwan. TSMC is preparing for a challenging period in the chip sector despite its strong recent financial performance.

title: Meta faces a future of more legal woes and falling revenues
summary: Meta, formerly Facebook, is experiencing significant challenges including plummeting stock value, falling revenues, and increasing regulatory scrutiny, a situation that worsened after its rebrand in October 2021. Despite investor concerns and substantial losses from its metaverse division, Reality Labs, CEO Mark Zuckerberg remains committed to heavy investment in the metaverse. The company also faces ongoing legal battles, hefty fines for data privacy breaches, and a class-action lawsuit settlement, exacerbating doubts about its future prospects.

title: Collective intelligence exponentially outperforms any one person or idea:" An interview with N-able's John Pagliuca
summary: John Pagliuca, CEO of N-able, discusses his support for Computing's Women in Tech Excellence Campaign, emphasizing the critical need for more women in the tech industry at all levels. He shares his career journey into IT and offers advice for women looking to enter or advance in tech, highlighting the importance of mentorship, continuous learning, and embracing uncomfortable challenges for growth. Pagliuca stresses that collective intelligence surpasses individual ideas and leaders should foster environments that encourage diverse feedback.

title: IonQ acquires quantum networking startup Entangled Networks
summary: IonQ Inc. has acquired Entangled Networks Ltd., a startup specializing in networking technology for linking quantum processors, for an undisclosed sum. This acquisition aims to advance IonQ's goal of building more advanced quantum systems with multiple processors by leveraging Entangled Networks' optical interconnect hardware and MultiQopt compiler software. The integration of Entangled Networks' expertise and tools is expected to lead to substantial performance improvements in IonQ's quantum hardware and support the development of prototype multi-processor systems this year.

title: Networked Quantum Computers: IonQ Acquires Assets of Entangled Networks
summary: IonQ, Inc. (NYSE: IONQ) announced its acquisition of the operating assets of Entangled Networks Ltd., a Toronto-based company specializing in distributed quantum processors. This acquisition, IonQ's first, is intended to further IonQ's goal of building large-scale quantum computers by enabling computation across multiple distributed quantum processors and strengthens IonQ's international presence with the launch of IonQ Canada. The Entangled Networks team will join IonQ, contributing expertise in quantum architecture and software tools to enhance system performance.

title: Intel Launches 4th Gen Xeon Scalable Processors, Max Series CPUs and GPUs
summary: Intel has launched its 4th Gen Xeon Scalable processors, along with the Intel Xeon CPU Max Series and Intel Data Center GPU Max Series. These new processors aim to deliver significant improvements in performance, efficiency, and capabilities for AI, cloud, network, edge, and high-performance computing, emphasizing built-in accelerators and sustainability features. The company highlights broad industry adoption and performance gains across various key workloads.

title: Intel 4th Gen Xeon series offers a leap in data center performance and efficiency
summary: Intel has launched its 4th Gen Intel Xeon scalable processors, including the Intel Xeon CPU Max Series and Intel Data Center GPU Max Series, featuring enhanced security and new AI capabilities. These processors promise significant improvements in data center performance and efficiency, offering workload-first acceleration and optimized software for better total cost of ownership. The new line boasts built-in accelerators, power savings, and expanded confidential computing features designed to address critical computing challenges and sustainability goals.

title: Are You Ready To Step Up To B2B Marketing’s New Destiny?
summary: B2B marketing is undergoing a significant transformation due to changes in buyer behavior, disruptive business models, and rapid technology evolution. Marketers must shift from traditional roles to a broader purpose focused on customer value and sustainable business growth. This requires strategic mindset shifts from product-centricity to customer outcomes, funnel to buyer's journey, and acquisition to lifecycle relationship management, emphasizing personalized, data-driven, and trust-building engagements.

title: WPP strengthens Salesforce expertise with Fenom Digital acquisition
summary: WPP has acquired Fenom Digital, a digital transformation agency specializing in Salesforce solutions, to bolster Wunderman Thompson's e-commerce capabilities. This acquisition aligns with a trend of agencies expanding their e-commerce offerings, particularly those with strong Salesforce ties, as online retail continues to grow. The move aims to enhance client services across multiple Salesforce clouds, despite recent economic struggles for Salesforce itself.

title: Salesforce to cut 10% of workforce in latest tech layoffs
summary: Salesforce Inc. announced it will cut 10% of its workforce and close some offices, aiming to reduce costs after rapid hiring during the pandemic. Co-CEO Marc Benioff stated the company hired "too many people" leading into the current economic downturn, taking responsibility for the over-hiring. This move follows similar workforce reductions by other tech giants like Meta and Amazon, as companies prepare for a potential deep downturn amid rising interest rates and a challenging economic environment.

title: CES: Intel Extends Performance Leadership with World's Fastest Mobile Processor
summary: At CES 2023, Intel launched its 13th Gen Intel Core mobile processor family, including the flagship Intel Core i9-13980HX, dubbed the world's fastest mobile processor and the first 24-core processor for a laptop. Intel also introduced new 13th Gen Intel Core desktop processors and the Intel Processor N-series for education and entry-level computing. These advancements aim to deliver superior performance, better battery life, and enhanced experiences across various computing segments, from enthusiast gaming laptops to thin-and-light devices and IoT applications.

title: HDFC Bank partners with Microsoft to drive its digital transformation efforts
summary: HDFC Bank has partnered with Microsoft to accelerate its digital transformation agenda, focusing on modernizing its data landscape, application portfolio, and enhancing enterprise security. The collaboration will leverage Microsoft's Azure cloud platform for a Federated Data Lake, enabling data monetization and democratizing access across business units. Additionally, HDFC Bank will utilize Microsoft Power Platform for app innovation and automation, and Microsoft 365 for a secure and collaborative digital workplace.

title: HDFC Bank partners with Microsoft as part of its digital transformation journey
summary: HDFC Bank is partnering with Microsoft to accelerate its digital transformation, focusing on modernizing its data landscape, enhancing employee productivity, and securing its enterprise with Microsoft Cloud. The collaboration involves leveraging Microsoft Azure for a Federated Data Lake, using Microsoft Power Platform to build an App Innovation and Automation Factory, and deploying Microsoft 365 and Security solutions to achieve a secure and integrated digital workplace. This initiative aims to provide a superior neo-banking experience for customers and support the bank's "Future Ready" strategy.

title: Apple’s market value drops below $2 trillion
summary: Apple Inc.'s market capitalization fell below $2 trillion for the first time since March 2021, driven by concerns over high inflation and a slowing global economy impacting demand for its products. This significant drop follows a year after the company briefly reached a $3 trillion valuation. Analysts have downgraded Apple due to anticipated supply chain issues and reduced consumer spending on high-end phones, forecasting a potential revenue decline.

title: Dynatrace Unveils DevSecOps Automation Partner Program
summary: Dynatrace has launched a new DevSecOps Automation Partner Program to integrate its software intelligence platform with over a dozen partner solutions, including GitLab, Gremlin, and PagerDuty. This initiative aims to automate tedious tasks in the software development lifecycle, improving speed to market and service resiliency for organizations. The program focuses on creating closed-loop automation through purpose-built integrations, making ecosystems run faster and smarter, and enabling solution providers to drive broader transformational efforts for customers.

title: Electronic Arts Names Chris Suh as Chief Financial Officer
summary: Electronic Arts Inc. has named Chris Suh as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective March 1, 2022. Suh joins EA from Microsoft, where he served as Corporate Vice President and CFO of the Cloud + AI group, bringing over 25 years of global finance leadership experience. He will report to Chairman and CEO Andrew Wilson and be responsible for EA's financial functions.

title: HP Inc. is cutting up to 6,000 employees as it becomes the latest tech company to announce major layoffs
summary: HP Inc. announced plans to lay off between 4,000 and 6,000 employees over the next three years, representing nearly 10% of its workforce. This decision is part of a cost-cutting strategy amidst declining sales, an 11.2% drop in fourth-quarter revenue to $14.8 billion, and a challenging economic environment exacerbated by high inflation and interest rates. The company expects the restructuring to save $1.4 billion annually by the end of fiscal year 2025, with costs estimated at $1 billion.

title: What Is A Snowflake Database? Introduction To Modern Data Platform
summary: This article provides an in-depth introduction to Snowflake, a modern cloud-independent data warehousing platform. It explains Snowflake's architecture, including its cloud services, query processing, and database storage layers, and highlights its numerous benefits like scalability, security, and seamless data sharing. The article also differentiates Snowflake from other data platforms based on architecture, maintenance, scalability, and cost.

title: Salesforce Inc. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: Salesforce Inc. (CRM) stock rose 0.94% on Tuesday, closing at $130.66, outperforming the broader market which saw mixed results. The company's stock achieved its second consecutive day of gains, despite being significantly below its 52-week high. Salesforce also outperformed competitors like Microsoft and Alphabet.

title: Gartner crowns Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, Check Point network firewalls leaders
summary: Gartner has recognized Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, and Check Point Software Technologies as leaders in its latest Magic Quadrant for Network Firewall report. The report highlights the evolution of network firewalls into hybrid-mesh firewalls with the rise of cloud firewalls and firewall-as-a-service (FWaaS) offerings, predicting that over 60% of organizations will use multiple firewall deployments by 2026. Gartner also identified other market players, including challengers, visionaries, and niche players.

title: How King and its Candy Crush IP will help Microsoft boost its mobile revenues
summary: Microsoft is attempting to convince the US FTC that its acquisition of Activision Blizzard would boost its mobile revenues significantly, with its share of global mobile gaming revenues potentially increasing from 0.3% to over 4%. A key driver of this growth is King, the developer behind Candy Crush, which was the largest contributor to Activision Blizzard's mobile growth in Q3 2022. While the FTC has filed a lawsuit to block the $68.7 billion deal over monopoly concerns, Microsoft argues that the acquisition of a single game studio cannot disrupt a highly competitive industry.

title: Microsoft, Cisco Shareholder Votes Demonstrate Increasing Investor Demand for Tax and Offshore Transparency
summary: Shareholders of Microsoft and Cisco, representing hundreds of billions in investments, voted in favor of proposals calling for public country-by-country reporting on offshore operations and tax practices. This trend indicates growing investor demand for transparency regarding potential risks associated with opaque offshore activities. The FACT Coalition highlights that public country-by-country reporting is becoming inevitable due to global momentum and regulatory considerations in jurisdictions like the EU, Australia, and the U.S.

title: 7 Cybersecurity Stocks to Buy and Hold for the Long Haul
summary: This article identifies seven cybersecurity stocks and an ETF that investors should consider buying and holding for the long haul, despite the current tech downturn. The author emphasizes the increasing essentiality of cybersecurity for businesses and governments, projecting significant market growth. Featured companies include Palo Alto Networks, Microsoft, Palantir, Zscaler, CrowdStrike Holdings, and Fortinet, alongside the Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG).

title: Kyndryl Receives Recognitions from ISG and Gartner® for Managed Network Services
summary: Kyndryl has been recognized by leading analyst firms ISG and Gartner for its network solutions and managed network services, just one year after becoming an independent company. This recognition highlights Kyndryl's growth strategy, advanced delivery, and strategic alliances with key partners like hyperscalers, Nokia, Intel, Cisco, and Vodafone. The company emphasizes its commitment to reskilling employees and delivering next-generation network technologies, including private wireless, edge computing, and cloud networking, to drive business transformation for its customers.

title: NetApp Develops Software to Unify Hybrid Multicloud Management
summary: NetApp has released BlueXP software, a unified control plane designed to simplify hybrid multicloud management for companies by automating operations across on-premises and public cloud environments. This new offering aims to address the complexity of modern diverse IT landscapes, providing a single point of visibility and management for various storage assets. BlueXP integrates an AIOps engine, AI-enabled health monitoring, advanced security features including a ransomware dashboard, and a pay-per-play model with NetApp Keystone services.

title: MSCI ONE Aims to Help Investors Turn Data Into Insights
summary: MSCI Inc. has launched MSCI ONE, an open architecture technology platform built on Microsoft Azure, designed to help investors convert vast amounts of data into actionable insights for investment decisions. The platform provides next-generation quantitative investment analytics through a modern web-based experience, combining flexible distribution, cloud delivery, dashboards, and visualizations. MSCI ONE offers single-point access to various services like MSCI Risk Insights, Climate Solutions, and its Developer Community, emphasizing improved client experience through transformational technology.

title: Tech: Micron looks past semiconductor downturn for opportunities, ramps up investment in Penang
summary: Micron Technology Inc. is navigating a semiconductor downturn characterized by inventory adjustments and weakened consumer demand but sees significant long-term growth opportunities driven by data-intensive technologies like AI and 5G. Despite current challenges, Micron is ramping up its investment in Penang, Malaysia, with an additional US$1 billion planned for a second factory, bringing its total investment in the Batu Kawan site to US$2 billion. The company emphasizes Malaysia's crucial role as a Centre of Excellence for its assembly and test operations and its commitment to continued expansion in the region.

title: Arqit Quantum Inc. Announces Financial and Operational Results for the Fiscal Year 2022
summary: Arqit Quantum Inc. announced its financial and operational results for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2022, reporting $20 million in revenue and other operating income. A significant technological innovation means the company no longer needs to build quantum satellites, leading to expected positive impacts on future financial results and a refocusing of its go-to-market strategy through major channel partnerships. The company also detailed key operational highlights, including integrations with Fortinet, Amazon Web Services, and Dell Technologies, and announced awards and progress in government markets.

title: Run SQL Server on EC2 using FSx for ONTAP
summary: This article discusses the benefits of running SQL Server on Amazon EC2 with FSx for NetApp ONTAP, highlighting how it addresses migration challenges from on-premises environments. It delves into various use cases, including simplified database backup and restore processes using NetApp SnapCenter, efficient test recovery, DevOps cloning, and disaster recovery/migration using SnapMirror. The integration provides enterprise-grade storage capabilities, high performance, and cost optimization for SQL workloads in the AWS cloud.

title: Why Kodak Died and Fujifilm Thrived: A Tale of Two Film Companies
summary: This article analyzes why Kodak, once a giant in the film industry, ultimately failed, while its competitor Fujifilm managed to thrive despite the digital revolution. It attributes Kodak's downfall to its inability to diversify beyond the declining photo industry and its misjudgment of the digital market's profitability. In contrast, Fujifilm successfully leveraged its existing technologies and pursued aggressive diversification into new markets like pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and highly functional materials, demonstrating a more adventurous and adaptable corporate culture.

title: Now, Near, Next: How Software Startups Can Accelerate Growth in Uncertain Times
summary: In uncertain economic times, software startups can leverage the "Now, Near, Next" framework to maintain agility and accelerate growth. This framework helps businesses assess current challenges, identify near-term focus areas, and plan for future market conditions. By implementing these strategies, startups can outperform competitors and prepare for accelerated growth when economic conditions improve.

title: Annual Shareholders Meeting 2022
summary: Microsoft's Annual Shareholders Meeting for 2022 covered financial performance, strategic priorities, and shareholder proposals. Key topics included record financial results in FY22, investments in AI and cloud computing, and responses to shareholder concerns regarding diversity, fair chance employment, climate change, government contracts, and tax transparency. The leadership team also discussed balancing strategic growth with cost management and the ongoing FTC lawsuit regarding the Activision Blizzard acquisition.

title: Microsoft acquires Lumenisity®, an innovator in hollow core fiber (HCF) cable
summary: Microsoft has acquired Lumenisity® Limited, a leader in hollow core fiber (HCF) solutions, to enhance its global cloud infrastructure and address the strict latency and security requirements of its Cloud Platform and Services customers. Lumenisity's HCF technology offers increased speed, lower latency, enhanced security, and lower costs compared to traditional fiber, benefiting sectors like healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, retail, and government. This acquisition will enable Microsoft to accelerate innovations in networking and infrastructure by integrating Lumenisity’s technology and expert team.

title: P&G Doubles Down on Digital Capacity and Shelf Orchestration With Supply Chain 3.0
summary: Procter & Gamble is heavily investing in its Supply Chain 3.0 strategy, leveraging emerging technologies and advanced algorithms to drive productivity, cost effectiveness, and market growth. This digital transformation includes partnerships with companies like Microsoft for a digital platform utilizing IoT, AI, machine learning, and edge computing to enhance visibility and real-time decision-making across its manufacturing sites globally. P&G is also applying these advancements to optimize shelf orchestration based on point-of-sale data and shopper behavior, aiming to improve on-shelf availability and the overall shopping experience.

title: Indian Engineering and Construction enterprises accelerate cloud adoption to enhance their customer experience
summary: Indian Engineering and Construction (E&C) enterprises are increasingly adopting SAP's cloud ERP solution, 'RISE with SAP,' to drive digital transformation, enhance customer experience, and become future-ready. Key players like Prestige Estates Projects, Pacific Development Corporation, and Nambiar Builders have already implemented RISE with SAP to simplify supply chains, finance processes, and achieve 100% uptime, highlighting a growing demand for cloud technology across the sector. This shift enables businesses to unlock new opportunities, improve operational efficacy, and become more agile and sustainable intelligent enterprises.

title: F.T.C. Sues to Block Microsoft’s $69 Billion Acquisition of Activision (Published 2022)
summary: The Federal Trade Commission has sued to block Microsoft's $69 billion acquisition of video game maker Activision Blizzard, citing concerns that the deal would harm consumers by allowing Microsoft to withhold popular games like Call of Duty from rivals. This aggressive move by the F.T.C. signals a stronger regulatory stance against the expansion of big tech companies. Microsoft has stated its intention to fight the lawsuit in court to proceed with the acquisition.

title: Rackspace Valuation Falls Below $1 Billion Amid MSP Ransomware Attack
summary: Rackspace Technology's market capitalization has fallen below $1 billion following a Hosted Exchange ransomware attack that disrupted email services for some customers. This cyberattack exacerbates existing business challenges, as the company's valuation has declined significantly from $8 billion in 2020 and its revenue growth lags behind the broader MSP and MSSP markets. Rackspace is now offering free Microsoft 365 services to impacted customers and undergoing a business realignment, with its future strategy potentially influenced by the attack.

title: Google, Oracle, Amazon, Microsoft to share $9 billion ‘return of JEDI’ defense contract
summary: Google, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft will jointly share a $9 billion hybrid contract from the Pentagon to provide secure cloud services globally. The contract, known as Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability, is scheduled for completion by June 8, 2028, with work to be performed in Reston, Va. This agreement follows previous discussions and changes regarding the Department of Defense's cloud computing needs.

title: AWS, Google, Microsoft and Oracle all get a piece of the Pentagon's $9B JWCC cloud computing contract
summary: The Pentagon has awarded Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Google, and Oracle shared portions of a $9 billion Joint Warfighting Cloud Capability (JWCC) contract, which will run through 2028. This multi-vendor approach replaces the previously controversial single-award JEDI contract and aligns with industry best practices of using multiple cloud providers for resilience and cost management. Analysts view this distributed award as a positive step, promoting competition and allowing the DOD to leverage the best capabilities of each cloud provider.

title: HPE GreenLake For Private Cloud Packs New AWS Kubernetes Punch
summary: HPE has enhanced its GreenLake for Private Cloud Enterprise platform, notably integrating with AWS’ Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) Anywhere. This expansion offers significant new services opportunities for partners and allows customers to deploy AWS Kubernetes in various private cloud environments. The updates also include new analytics for multi-cloud consumption, six new workload-optimized instances, and planned integrations with other Kubernetes platforms like Red Hat OpenShift.

title: For HPE, The Cloud Is A Private And A Public Matter
summary: HPE is focusing on its GreenLake utility platform to expand its presence in the hybrid cloud market, emphasizing private cloud offerings. The company aims to make its entire portfolio available as a service and is seeing steady growth in GreenLake's orders and revenue. HPE is enhancing GreenLake with new services like Private Cloud Enterprise and expanding partner offerings, catering to businesses that prefer a mix of public and private cloud solutions, especially for edge computing needs.

title: Introduction: Chuck Gahun, Principal Analyst For Content Management And Digital Experience Technology
summary: Chuck Gahun joins Forrester as Principal Analyst for Content Management and Digital Experience Technology, focusing on the intersection of content technologies and digital business strategy. His research will explore competitive digital business strategies, emphasizing the critical role of content in customer acquisition and growth, and the development of digital experience ecosystems. Gahun brings over 30 years of digital and agency experience to his new role.

title: Email hosting service Rackspace says it's facing a ransomware attack
summary: Rackspace Technology, a major cloud and email hosting provider, announced a ransomware attack is responsible for a widespread outage that has kept some customers from their email inboxes since Friday. The company revealed the attack may lead to revenue loss for its Hosted Exchange business and has hired a cyber defense firm to investigate, but cannot provide a restoration timeline. Customers are complaining about a lack of communication and support as they are advised to migrate to Microsoft 365, with concerns about data security and the difficulty of the migration process.

title: Rackspace Security Incident Causes Thousands To Lose Email Service
summary: Thousands of Rackspace customers lost email service after a security incident caused a weekend-long outage impacting its hosted Exchange. Rackspace began restoring services to Microsoft 365 customers and confirmed the incident was security-related, advising a move to Microsoft 365 for affected users. The incident led to significant customer frustration and a 10 percent drop in Rackspace's stock.

title: Nutanix buyout may be on the cards with HPE sniffing around
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is reportedly considering acquiring hyperconverged infrastructure vendor Nutanix, with discussions ongoing for several months. The potential acquisition aligns with HPE's GreenLake everything-as-a-service (XaaS) platform strategy, aiming to enhance its software offerings and attract more customers. Nutanix's recent financial recovery and improved market cap make it an attractive target, especially given HPE's struggles in expanding the GreenLake model to its global partners.

title: Salesforce shares tumble after surprise exit of co-CEO Taylor
summary: Salesforce Inc (CRM.N) shares fell by about 10% after co-CEO Bret Taylor's unexpected departure, raising concerns about the company's co-CEO leadership model and slowing revenue growth. This exit prompted at least 17 brokerages to cut their price targets on the stock, with analysts noting it as a significant blow given Taylor's leadership role in product development. Taylor's departure comes after just one year in the co-CEO role, leaving co-founder Marc Benioff as the sole top boss.

title: Vodafone Picks Dubber for UK and European Business Strategy
summary: Vodafone Group PLC has partnered with Dubber, a Melbourne-based conversational intelligence and unified recording company, to deliver direct recording and AI services across its mobile networks for business customers in the UK and Europe, starting with Germany. This collaboration will leverage Dubber's platform to provide enhanced compliance and data insights across mobile and UC services, including RingCentral, Cisco Webex, and Microsoft Teams. The initiative aims to expand Vodafone's existing recording subscriber base and generate accretive revenue for Dubber by offering automated, self-service next-generation recordings and personalized customer experiences.

title: Global investment banking firm blazes new trail to remote work with complete cloud-delivered security
summary: Jefferies, a global investment banking firm, has successfully transitioned its entire global workforce to a secure remote work environment by leveraging Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Access. This cloud-delivered security platform addressed challenges related to complexity, risk, and data loss prevention in a hybrid work model, particularly accelerated by the pandemic. The solution enabled Jefferies to unify security policies, provide a seamless user experience, and ensure the protection of highly sensitive client data across its worldwide operations.

title: HPE is in talks to buy Nutanix: Report
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is reportedly in discussions to acquire cloud computing firm Nutanix. This potential acquisition could establish HPE as a dominant force in the cloud computing market and allow it to cross-sell growth-oriented software to its extensive customer base. Experts suggest that while the deal could benefit HPE with lower operational costs and a larger market share, customers might face higher pricing for cloud services post-acquisition.

title: Sony expects profit to slip despite record PlayStation 5 sales
summary: Sony Group Corp forecasts a 3.2% decline in operating profit for the current business year, despite expecting a record 25 million PlayStation 5 sales. This profit slip is attributed to weaker financial services sales, which are offsetting gains from its gaming, music, and movie divisions. While the gaming unit shows strong console sales, a decline in more profitable videogame software sales and a drop in image sensor profit are contributing to the overall profit reduction.

title: LinkedIn Business Highlights from Microsoft’s FY23 Q3 Earnings
summary: LinkedIn's revenue increased by 8% year-over-year in Q3 FY23, with member growth accelerating for the seventh consecutive quarter, reaching over 930 million members globally. The platform saw significant expansion in India, a 73% increase in Gen Z student sign-ups, and continued success in Talent Solutions and Marketing Solutions. LinkedIn is also becoming a hub for AI learning and features, offering over 100 AI courses and new AI-powered tools.

title: Problems at Hercules Capital (HTGC)
summary: The Bear Cave challenges Hercules Capital's perceived strength, alleging that its robust financial appearance is a "mirage." The report highlights concerning portfolio marks, severe distress in portfolio companies, and significant stock declines in its past successful investments. Despite management's optimistic outlook and analyst endorsements, the article raises questions about the true health of Hercules Capital's $2.8 billion loan portfolio.

title: Improve DNS Security with Zscaler's New Innovations
summary: Zscaler has announced significant innovations to its DNS security module, enhancing security, availability, flexibility, and performance. The updates include DNS encryption via DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH), improved failover capabilities, better DNS tunnel protection, enhanced DGA detection, and protective DNS enablement for government agencies. These features aim to address the pervasive issue of DNS-related attacks and provide organizations with a more robust, cloud-native solution for secure and efficient DNS resolution.

title: 2023 Phishing Report shows 47.2% more attacks
summary: The Zscaler ThreatLabz 2023 Phishing Report reveals a significant 47.2% surge in phishing attacks in 2022 due to increasingly sophisticated techniques and the use of AI tools. The report highlights that education was the most targeted sector, with Microsoft brands and crypto exchanges being frequently exploited. It recommends adopting a Zero Trust architecture and educating employees to combat these evolving threats.

title: Chegg announces CheggMate, the new AI companion, built with GPT-4
summary: Chegg, Inc. announced CheggMate, a new AI-enhanced learning service built with OpenAI’s GPT-4, designed to provide personalized and interactive learning experiences for students. CheggMate will leverage Chegg's proprietary data and GPT-4's problem-solving capabilities to offer features like tailored quizzes, guided support, and recommendations. Early access for students is expected in May 2023.

title: Viasat real-time Earth antennas integrated on Microsoft Azure Orbital
summary: Viasat Inc. and Microsoft Azure Orbital have integrated Viasat's Real-Time Earth (RTE) ground service with Azure, making it accessible through the Azure marketplace. This collaboration equips five RTE sites with high-speed connectivity directly to the Azure cloud, offering commercial satellite operators secure, high-throughput, and low-latency connectivity for their spacecraft. The solution supports Ka-band transmissions, which are crucial for high downlink rates from remote sensing missions and aims to reduce data delivery times.

title: Gartner: Top 5 Markets In $4.6 Trillion Tech Industry For 2023, 2024
summary: Gartner projects global IT spending to reach $4.6 trillion in 2023, increasing over 5% annually, despite economic challenges like inflation. The top five market segments for spending are communications services, software, devices, data center systems, and IT services, with software and IT services showing significant growth. The sustained demand is driven by digital transformation and a shortage of skilled IT experts, leading companies to prioritize software and external IT services.

title: SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) Stock: Breakout Leveraging Tech Stocks Rally?
summary: The SPDR S&P 500 (SPY) ETF has shown a positive resurgence in 2023, largely driven by gains in tech and semiconductor stocks, which comprise a significant portion of its portfolio. Technical analysis suggests a potential bullish breakout for SPY, with indicators pointing to an upcoming rally. Investors are advised to watch support levels and anticipate a rise leveraging the strength of its underlying tech holdings.

title: Laura Fritzlen Joins Zscaler as Public Sector Alliances & Channels VP
summary: Laura Fritzlen has been appointed as Vice President of Public Sector Alliances & Channels at Zscaler, a cloud security company. With over two decades of experience, Fritzlen will focus on expanding strategic partner relationships and alliances within the public sector to drive collaboration and growth. She previously held leadership roles at ServiceNow, Symantec, and Dell EMC.

title: Investment Giant Fidelity Offers New Metaverse and Crypto Payments ETFs
summary: Fidelity Investments, managing over $4.2 trillion in assets, has launched two new ETFs: the Fidelity Crypto Industry and Digital Payments ETF (FDIG) and the Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET). These new offerings aim to expand Fidelity's presence in the digital ecosystem, catering to growing investor demand, especially from younger demographics, for exposure to crypto and metaverse industries. While FDIG does not offer direct crypto exposure, it invests in companies supporting the digital asset ecosystem, and FMET focuses on companies building out the metaverse.

title: Microsoft cuts over 500 jobs in another round of tech layoffs
summary: Microsoft has laid off 559 workers in Bellevue and Redmond, bringing their regional total to over 2,700 jobs cut since January. This follows a previous round of layoffs in February and reflects a broader trend of job cuts across the tech industry, with companies like Meta and Amazon also reducing their workforces. Overall, U.S. tech companies have shed more than 300,000 jobs in recent months.

title: Rackspace cutting workforce in response to downturn. Amid string of losses, its stock has plummeted.
summary: Rackspace Technology Inc. is laying off nearly 4 percent of its global workforce, approximately 275 employees, in response to a broad economic downturn. This decision comes as the company's stock has plummeted more than 80 percent in the last year, including a significant drop after a December ransomware attack. Rackspace is also struggling with a string of quarterly losses despite record revenues, and its CEO is implementing a new business strategy.

title: Rackspace Lays Off 275 Employees As Stock Hits Bottom
summary: Rackspace Technology announced it is laying off 275 employees, approximately 4% of its global workforce, due to an uncertain economic climate and the need to align its cost structure with business demands. This decision comes as the company's stock has plummeted by 84% over the past year, trading at a near-all-time low of $1.76 per share, and after reporting an $805 million net loss in 2022 and experiencing a ransomware attack in December. Rackspace joins a growing list of tech companies implementing significant layoffs in 2023 amid a broader industry downturn.

title: Memory chipmaker Micron expects revenue drop, expects AI to boost sales in 2025
summary: Micron Technology expects a significant revenue drop for its third quarter, in line with Wall Street predictions, but anticipates a strong recovery in 2025 driven by artificial intelligence. The company plans to reduce investments and cut headcount while emphasizing its strong position to capitalize on the growing demand for memory chips in AI servers. Despite near-term challenges, Micron is proceeding with new factory constructions and sees improving customer inventories and supply-demand balance.

title: Japanese regulator clears Microsoft’s acquisition of Activision Blizzard, sees no substantial harm to competition
summary: The Japan Fair Trade Commission has approved Microsoft's proposed $68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard, concluding it is unlikely to substantially restrain competition. This approval is significant as Japan is home to Sony, a vocal critic of the deal. While approved in Japan and several other countries, the merger is still under review by regulators in Europe and the US.

title: Zoom jumps on ChatGPT bandwagon, integrates generative AI features
summary: Zoom is incorporating OpenAI's generative AI, the technology behind ChatGPT and GPT-4, into its video communications platform. These new features will generate Zoom Team Chat and email responses, and an AI feature for Zoom IQ will create shareable meeting summaries and whiteboard presentations. While initial availability is limited to select customers and specific products, Zoom plans a broader release, aiming to bolster its enterprise customer base through AI and automation.

title: Microsoft Israel to lay off dozens as part of global cutbacks
summary: Microsoft Israel is preparing to lay off dozens of employees, impacting its cyber team for the first time, as part of Microsoft's broader global restructuring which includes 10,000 job cuts announced in January. The Israeli R&D center, employing about 2,700 people with half in cybersecurity, will see these layoffs primarily affect its security organization, with an estimated 10% reduction. This move follows other recent high-tech layoffs in Israel.

title: AB US Low Volatility Equity ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the AB US Low Volatility Equity ETF (LOWV), which was established on March 22, 2023. The ETF focuses on large- and mid-cap US stocks, actively managed to achieve lower volatility than the broader market. Key holdings include major technology companies like Alphabet, Microsoft, Apple, NVIDIA, and Amazon, alongside diversified investments across various sectors.

title: NICE Achieves Milestone of One Million Agents on CXone
summary: NICE has reached a significant milestone with one million agents and supervisors now using its CXone cloud platform, following its recognition by Gartner and integration of OpenAI's generative modeling. The company reported strong financial results for 2022, including a 10% increase in total revenue and 26% growth in cloud revenue, securing several eight-figure deals. NICE projects continued growth for 2023, leveraging its strong market position, cloud expansion, and AI advancements.

title: Lumen’s Exec Team Taking The Provider From ‘Channel-Friendly’ To ‘Channel-Focused’
summary: Lumen Technologies is transitioning from a "channel-friendly" to a "channel-focused" organization, driven by a new C-suite with strong channel backgrounds. This shift involves significant internal investments in strategic services and a greater emphasis on customer experience, with partners playing a crucial role. The company's leadership is actively engaging with partners and expanding its partner programs to foster growth and improve collaboration.

title: Demo of China’s Answer to ChatGPT Disappoints Investors
summary: Baidu Inc.'s CEO Robin Li unveiled "Ernie Bot," China's answer to ChatGPT, in a recorded video demonstration that disappointed investors, leading to a 6.4% drop in Baidu's shares. The pre-recorded nature of the demo and lack of real-time interaction raised questions about Ernie's capabilities compared to OpenAI's ChatGPT. Despite the initial disappointment, Baidu is considered a frontrunner in China's AI race, planning to integrate Ernie Bot across its services while navigating concerns about US tech restrictions and Chinese regulatory oversight.

title: China’s Answer to ChatGPT Gets an Artificial Debut and Disappoints (Published 2023)
summary: Baidu's debut of its ChatGPT rival, Ernie, disappointed investors after its "live" demonstration was revealed to be prerecorded, causing Baidu's shares to tumble. This event highlights China's ongoing efforts to catch up with the United States in AI development, particularly given restrictions on high-end computing chips. The botched rollout also points to the intensive global race in large language model technology, dominated by a few major players.

title: Morgan Stanley partners with OpenAI on internal chatbot for its advisors
summary: Morgan Stanley is partnering with OpenAI to create an internal-facing chatbot for its financial advisors, leveraging OpenAI's latest GPT-4 technology. This chatbot will provide advisors with instant, accurate answers generated exclusively from Morgan Stanley's proprietary content library, aiming to enhance efficiency and client service. This initiative is part of the firm's broader exploration into AI-powered tools, though Morgan Stanley emphasizes that human advice and advisor-client relationships will remain central to its wealth management strategy.

title: Using the power of Cloudflare’s global network to detect malicious domains using machine learning
summary: Cloudflare leverages its global network and machine learning to detect malicious domains, focusing on two key threat techniques: Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs) and DNS tunneling. The company uses advanced neural networks, including transformer-based models and gradient-boosted decision trees, to classify and identify these threats. Their system processes all DNS queries through the 1.1.1.1 resolver to swiftly identify and mitigate these evolving cyber threats.

title: Smart move: Artificial intelligence and 3D laser scanning for MEP applications
summary: This article explores how artificial intelligence (AI) and 3D laser scanning can significantly benefit Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) applications. It highlights how 3D laser scanning provides crucial accurate data for new construction or retrofitting projects, while AI can then process this data for pattern recognition, identifying optimal and energy-efficient solutions, and enhancing project management. The combination of these technologies, along with human expertise, is presented as a powerful tool for improving efficiency and decision-making in MEP design and implementation.

title: PETRONAS
summary: PETRONAS, a global oil and gas company, partnered with IBM Consulting to develop the UP app, accelerating project completion by up to four times. This digital solution provides decision-makers with fast access to curated upstream data, enhancing operational efficiency and decision-making within the company. The UP platform, built using agile methodologies on Microsoft Azure, now serves over 30,000 users and features more than 100 diverse functionalities, significantly impacting PETRONAS's digital transformation.

title: Microsoft adding to far West Side data center with $175.9 million expansion project this year
summary: Microsoft is planning a $175.9 million expansion of its data center in San Antonio's Texas Research Park, dubbed "SAT40." Construction on the 153,227-square-foot facility is set to begin in June and finish in September 2023. This is the latest in a series of data center investments by Microsoft in the area, driven by increasing demand for cloud technology despite recent company-wide layoffs.

title: Einstein AI was good, but Salesforce claims Einstein GPT is even better
summary: Salesforce announced a new partnership with OpenAI and launched its Einstein GPT generative AI service, aiming to enhance CRM, marketing, and sales processes. Einstein GPT integrates proprietary AI models with external generative AI, initially with OpenAI, to automate content generation and improve customer experience. The company also introduced a $250 million fund through Salesforce Ventures to support the generative AI startup ecosystem.

title: Rackspace Technology appoints Dr Angela Kurien Murze as Cloud Innovation Centre India Head
summary: Rackspace Technology has appointed Dr. Angela Kurien Murze as the Head of its Cloud Innovation Centre in India. Based in Pune, Dr. Murze will lead the Global Delivery team and is expected to drive profitability, overseeing pre-sales, delivery, alliances, and marketing. Her appointment is part of a broader executive team expansion aimed at accelerating global cloud business growth.

title: How legal teams are using Luminance for AI-powered automation
summary: This article details how legal teams are leveraging Luminance, an AI-powered automation platform, to streamline contract generation and review processes, reduce costs, and free up legal professionals for higher-value work. Examples include IDEXX Laboratories using Luminance to quickly review contracts for connections to sanctioned entities and Koch Industries automating NDA and master service agreement generation. The platform is also adopted by the Big Four accounting firms, like Deloitte, to assist clients in contract standardization projects, achieving significant time savings.

title: 10 Undervalued, High-Quality Stocks With Competitive Advantages
summary: This article identifies 10 undervalued, high-quality stocks with wide economic moats, according to Morningstar analysts. These companies, including Adobe, Microsoft, and Alphabet, have strong balance sheets, high profitability, and competitive advantages expected to last over 20 years. The stocks listed were trading below their fair value estimates as of March 2, 2023.

title: WEBTOON and LINE Studio Announce March 14 Launch Date for the True Beauty Mobile Puzzle Game
summary: WEBTOON and LINE Studio have announced that the "True Beauty" mobile puzzle game will launch globally on March 14, available on Google Play and Apple App Store. The game is based on the popular webcomic "True Beauty," which has accumulated over six billion views, and will feature puzzle-style gameplay, fan-favorite characters, and customizable upgrades. Pre-registration for the game is currently open, offering limited edition in-game rewards.

title: Microsoft’s venture arm M12 is undergoing a big strategy shift—and insiders have left the fund
summary: Microsoft's venture arm, M12, is shifting its strategy from a primarily financial corporate venture capital model to a more strategic, Microsoft-aligned approach. This change emphasizes integrating startups with Microsoft's ecosystem rather than focusing solely on financial returns, leading to significant internal adjustments and the departure of at least eight employees since mid-2021. The shift aims to deepen M12's focus on innovation, aligning with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's vision, particularly in areas like AI.

title: GLOF Top Holdings List & Exposure (iShares Global Equity Factor ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings, geographic, currency, sector, industry, and sub-industry exposures for the iShares Global Equity Factor ETF (GLOF). It highlights that NVIDIA, Apple, and Alphabet are the top three holdings, making up a significant portion of the fund's total assets. The ETF primarily invests in the United States and has its largest exposure to the Technology sector, particularly in Semiconductors.

title: CEO Antonio Neri On HPE’s Supercomputing ChatGPT Advantage, Axis Security And GreenLake Momentum
summary: HPE CEO Antonio Neri discusses the company's strong position to capitalize on the ChatGPT frenzy through its Supercomputing-as-a-Service offering, driven by its acquisition of Cray Supercomputer. He also highlights HPE's expanded edge portfolio with the acquisition of Axis Security, integrating it into the GreenLake platform for a comprehensive SASE model. Neri emphasizes the significant growth in HPE GreenLake's annualized revenue run rate and total contract value, underscoring the success of its as-a-service strategy and partner adoption.

title: C3 AI Announces Fiscal Third Quarter 2023 Financial Results
summary: C3 AI (NYSE: AI) announced strong financial results for its fiscal third quarter ended January 31, 2023, exceeding revenue guidance with $66.7 million. The company highlighted successful partnerships, expansion into new markets, and a confident outlook towards profitability in FY24, driven by its consumption-based pricing model and innovations in enterprise AI and Generative AI.

title: Three Times a Leader: CrowdStrike Named a Leader in Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Endpoint Protection Platforms
summary: CrowdStrike has been recognized as a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Protection Platforms (EPP) for the third consecutive time. The company's Falcon platform is highlighted for its comprehensive protection across endpoints, cloud workloads, and identity, along with its industry-leading EDR capabilities. CrowdStrike continues to focus on innovation to help organizations defend against cyberattacks and achieve a strong cybersecurity posture.

title: C3 AI Announces Fiscal Third Quarter 2023 Financial Results
summary: C3 AI announced strong financial results for its fiscal third quarter ended January 31, 2023, exceeding revenue guidance with $66.7 million. The company reported progress in its transition to a consumption-based pricing model, expanded its partner ecosystem with Google Cloud, AWS, Azure, Booz Allen, Accenture, EY, Peraton, and Baker Hughes, and highlighted significant innovation in enterprise AI and generative AI. C3 AI also re-emphasized its commitment to achieving cash positive and non-GAAP profitable status by the end of FY24.

title: HP CEO Lores: Hybrid Work Is ‘Driving Innovation Across Our Portfolio’
summary: HP CEO Enrique Lores stated that hybrid work is a long-term trend fueling innovation across their portfolio, with their hybrid systems business more than doubling year over year. Despite a general economic downturn and weakening corporate demand impacting PC sales, the company maintains its fiscal year outlook and expects to achieve significant cost savings. HP is also expanding its subscription services and investing in areas like AI and professional workstations.

title: PRF Top Holdings List & Exposure (Invesco RAFI US 1000 ETF)
summary: This article provides a detailed breakdown of the Invesco RAFI US 1000 ETF (PRF) holdings. It lists the top 25 stock holdings, including Alphabet, Apple, and Microsoft, which collectively account for 34.92% of the fund. The report also outlines PRF's geographic, currency, sector, industry, and sub-industry exposures, with a primary focus on the United States and the Technology and Financials sectors.

title: News | CBRE Taps Ex-Microsoft Environmental Strategist To Lead Brokerage's Sustainability Efforts
summary: CBRE, the world's largest commercial real estate services firm, has appointed Robert Bernard, formerly Microsoft's chief environmental strategist, as its new chief sustainability officer. Bernard will be responsible for enhancing CBRE's sustainability services for clients and helping the company achieve its carbon-reduction goals. This strategic hire comes as real estate firms increasingly focus on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) commitments amidst economic challenges.

title: The Future of AI Stocks: 7 Companies to Keep Your Eye On
summary: This article identifies seven key AI stocks and ETFs that investors should consider due to artificial intelligence's potential to revolutionize various industries. It highlights companies like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Advanced Micro Devices for their direct involvement in AI technology, along with Innodata and C3.ai for their specific AI solutions. Additionally, it suggests AI-focused ETFs like ROBO Global Artificial Intelligence ETF and Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF for diversified investment in the burgeoning AI sector.

title: Should You Fund Your 401(k) First or Your IRA?
summary: This article discusses the optimal order for funding retirement accounts, including 401(k)s, IRAs, and HSAs, and also covers recent financial news. It highlights the impending expiration of Vanguard's hybrid ETF/mutual fund patent and its potential impact on the fund market, along with earnings reports from Kraft Heinz, Roku, and Cisco Systems. The experts provide a hierarchy for allocating retirement savings, emphasizing employer match, HSAs, Roth IRAs, and then evaluating company 401(k)s.

title: As chatbots boom, Nvidia sales outlook beats Wall Street expectations
summary: Nvidia Corp (NVDA.O) surpassed Wall Street's first-quarter revenue expectations, driven by a surge in demand for its chips used in AI services like chatbots. The company announced a new cloud computing service to help businesses develop generative AI, positioning itself to significantly benefit from the growing AI sector despite a broader downturn in the PC market. Analysts project this boom in generative AI could add an additional $14 billion to Nvidia's revenue by 2027.

title: Meet the $10,000 Nvidia chip powering the race for A.I.
summary: The Nvidia A100 chip, costing around $10,000, has become a critical tool in the artificial intelligence industry, powering applications like ChatGPT and Stable Diffusion. Nvidia dominates the market for GPUs used in machine learning, with the A100 serving as a "workhorse" for AI professionals and requiring substantial investment for companies to train and deploy AI models. Despite the high costs and emerging competition, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang asserts that their GPUs offer a much more affordable solution for developing sophisticated AI models compared to traditional CPU-based data centers.

title: Nvidia adds to AI hype with new cloud-based service, stock jumps on forecast
summary: Nvidia's shares surged after the company announced strong fiscal fourth-quarter results and plans to make its AI software available on major cloud platforms like Oracle, Microsoft, and Alphabet. CEO Jensen Huang highlighted the potential of their new browser-based DGX Cloud AI supercomputer service to accelerate adoption of higher-margin data-center software, capitalizing on the booming interest in artificial intelligence. This move is expected to expand the chip maker's revenue streams beyond hardware.

title: Ansys Inc. stock rises Wednesday, outperforms market
summary: Ansys Inc. (ANSS) stock increased by 0.36% on Wednesday, closing at $266.78, despite a broader market decline where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both fell. This rise ended a three-day losing streak for the company's shares. Ansys outperformed competitors like Microsoft Corp. and International Business Machines Corp., and its trading volume also exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Nvidia earnings overshadowed by Microsoft, ChatGPT, OpenAI, 10-year gaming partnership
summary: Nvidia's upcoming earnings report is largely overshadowed by its new 10-year partnership with Microsoft to bring Activision Blizzard and Xbox games to GeForce Now. This partnership also highlights Nvidia's role in powering AI technologies like OpenAI's ChatGPT, especially given Microsoft's recent investment in OpenAI and plans to integrate its AI across services. The focus is now on Nvidia's data-center sales and its contribution from public cloud providers such as Microsoft Azure.

title: Microsoft teams up with Nvidia and Nintendo in 10-year deal to stream Xbox games
summary: Microsoft has secured 10-year agreements with Nvidia and Nintendo to stream Xbox games as part of its strategy to address antitrust concerns regarding its proposed acquisition of Activision Blizzard. This partnership aims to make Xbox and potential Activision titles available on Nvidia's GeForce Now cloud gaming service and Nintendo platforms, covering various devices. The move is intended to placate regulators scrutinizing the $69 billion deal.

title: Growth-Stock Funds Fly High but Fall Short in 2023′s First Half
summary: Growth-stock funds experienced a strong rebound in the first half of 2023 after significant losses in 2022, with large-growth funds doubling small-growth funds' gains. However, two-thirds of U.S.-centric active managers underperformed stylistically relevant indexes and passive rivals due to untimely sector allocations and light stakes in mega-cap stocks that drove market performance. International and emerging markets showed more modest gains, with some regions outperforming others, leading to a mixed bag for global stocks.

title: Apple makes history as first $3 trillion company amid tech stock surge
summary: Apple Inc. achieved a historic milestone, becoming the first company to reach a $3 trillion market value, driven by investor optimism about its expansion into new markets and a projected easing of interest rate hikes. This accomplishment is set against a backdrop of a broader tech stock surge, with other companies like Tesla and Nvidia also seeing significant gains due to advancements in AI and strategic partnerships. The article highlights Apple's strong financial performance and its reputation as a safe investment, alongside the success of other tech giants.

title: Q3 Stock Market Outlook: Time to Batten Down the Hatches or Raise the Sail?
summary: Morningstar's Q3 2023 stock market outlook suggests that while the U.S. market is still undervalued, the margin of safety has decreased, and the rally in the first half of the year has been disproportionately driven by a few "Magnificent Seven" stocks. Investors are advised to take profits from overextended growth and technology stocks and reallocate to undervalued sectors like communications and real estate, and to value, mid-cap, and small-cap stocks. The outlook anticipates slower market gains due to economic slowdown, tight monetary policy, and reduced credit availability, but expects any future pullbacks to be relatively shallow.

title: XPeng Announces G6 Ultra Smart Coupe SUV
summary: XPeng Inc. has launched its G6 Ultra Smart Coupe SUV in China, built on the SEPA2.0 architecture and priced from 209,900 RMB to 276,900 RMB, with deliveries starting in July 2023. This vehicle features advanced ADAS (XNGP), an 800V powertrain (XPower), integrated aluminum die-casting, and CIB battery-body integration. The G6 boasts a 755 km range, fast-charging capabilities, and a sophisticated design, aiming to solidify XPeng's leadership in the smart EV market.

title: Apple’s market value ends above $3 trillion for the first time
summary: Apple Inc.'s market value surpassed $3 trillion for the first time at the close of a trading session, driven by positive inflation data and confidence in its market expansion strategies. This milestone reflects a 49 percent gain in Apple shares for 2023, amid a tech stock rebound fueled by expectations of slower interest rate hikes from the US Federal Reserve and buzz around artificial intelligence. The company's financial resilience, strong balance sheet, and a recent augmented-reality headset launch contribute to its success, making it one of only five US companies with a valuation exceeding $1 trillion.

title: The Best QQQ Stocks To Buy Now
summary: The article identifies nine top-performing tech and tech-adjacent stocks within the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF, highlighting their growth, innovation, and involvement in artificial intelligence. It details each company's industry, market value, and key factors contributing to its strong performance and future potential, especially in the context of AI advancements. The QQQ ETF itself is noted for its strong returns compared to the S&P 500 over various timeframes.

title: Chipmaker Micron beats on demand from booming AI, easing glut
summary: Micron Technology exceeded third-quarter revenue estimates driven by high demand for its memory chips in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence sector and an easing supply glut in traditional markets. The company's shares rose over 2% after reporting stronger-than-expected earnings and anticipating improved pricing trends. Despite ongoing U.S.-China tech tensions impacting its presence in the Chinese market, Micron expressed confidence in the memory industry's recovery.

title: Nvidia stock falls after CFO says no material impact from prospective wider ban on AI chip sales to China
summary: Nvidia's stock dropped after its CFO, Collette Kress, stated that an expanded U.S. ban on AI chip sales to China would likely have no immediate material impact on the company. However, Kress expressed concern about the long-term effects, suggesting it could lead to a "permanent loss of opportunities" globally. This statement followed reports that the Biden administration was considering widening export bans on AI technology to China.

title: Nvidia and AMD shares fall on report of new U.S. ban on AI chip exports to China
summary: Shares of Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. dropped following a report that the Biden administration is considering a new ban on sales of AI chips to China. This potential ban comes despite Nvidia managing to avoid $400 million in lost sales last year after a previous ban on some chip sales to China. The news impacted both companies with Nvidia shares falling 3% after hours and AMD shares also decreasing by 3%.

title: Active Growth ETF TGRW Doubling Returns of SPY
summary: The T. Rowe Price Growth Stock ETF (TGRW) has demonstrated strong performance in the first half of 2023, doubling the year-to-date returns of the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) with 32.1% compared to SPY's 15.8%. TGRW, which focuses on firms with strong cash flow and above-average earnings growth, is approaching its three-year anniversary and has seen substantial AUM growth. This active growth ETF is outperforming its benchmark thanks to its investment strategy and a competitive expense ratio of 52 basis points.

title: KT to invest $5.4 bn by 2027 to develop AI platforms
summary: South Korea’s telecom service provider KT Corp. plans to invest 7 trillion won ($5.4 billion) by 2027 to become the country’s leading AI service provider, focusing on the robot, healthcare, and education markets. The investment will be allocated to securing super AI source technologies, upgrading related infrastructure, and developing AI service models. KT aims to generate 1.3 trillion won ($1 billion) in revenue from five AI-related service areas by 2025: contact centers, logistics, robots, healthcare, and education.

title: InfraCap Equity Income Fund ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (ICAP)
summary: The InfraCap Equity Income Fund ETF (ICAP) holds an aggregate "Moderate Buy" rating with a price target of $27.48. This rating is based on 512 analyst ratings for 21 companies, representing 64.9% of the ETF's portfolio. The article provides a detailed breakdown of the top 21 holdings within the ETF, including their weight, individual consensus ratings, price targets, and potential upside.

title: Fidelity Disruptive Technology ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (FDTX)
summary: This article provides a review and aggregate rating for the Fidelity Disruptive Technology ETF (FDTX). MarketBeat calculates this rating by considering the weighted sentiment of analyst ratings for the ETF's constituent stocks. FDTX currently holds a "Moderate Buy" aggregate rating with an average predicted price target reflecting its current share price, based on analyst coverage of 22 companies.

title: Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF Review and Aggregate Rating (METV)
summary: This article provides an aggregate rating and price target for the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) based on Wall Street analyst ratings of its holdings. METV has an aggregate rating of "Moderate Buy" and a price target of $16.79, derived from 595 analyst ratings covering 18 companies within its portfolio. The top holdings include tech giants like Apple, Roblox, NVIDIA, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms, along with their individual analyst ratings and potential upsides.

title: The A.I. Race Is Now Between Two Chip Giants Led by Taiwanese American CEOs
summary: The generative A.I. boom has intensified competition between semiconductor giants Nvidia and AMD, who are racing to produce advanced A.I. chips. AMD recently announced the MI300X, a direct competitor to Nvidia's H100, aiming to challenge Nvidia's dominant market share in the A.I. chip sector. Both companies are led by Taiwanese American CEOs, Jensen Huang of Nvidia and Lisa Su of AMD, who share similar backgrounds and have played pivotal roles in their companies' success in the semiconductor industry.

title: Fidelity Disruptive Communications ETF
summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the Fidelity Disruptive Communications ETF (FDCF), including its price, holdings, expenses, performance, and ESG scores. The ETF tracks an active, no-index strategy focusing on global internet and communication sectors, with top holdings in companies like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms. It aims to offer investors exposure to disruptive communication technologies, detailing various metrics for financial advisors and investors.

title: AMD is chasing down Nvidia in AI, but one analyst worries the company is ‘somewhat late’
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) is pursuing the lucrative AI data-center market, estimated to be worth $150 billion, following recent product announcements. While many analysts praised AMD's efforts, Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon expressed concerns that AMD is "somewhat late" to the AI race compared to rival Nvidia Corp. Rasgon noted that AMD's AI discussion offered limited "hard numbers" and a timeline that seemed delayed relative to the competition.

title: AMD launches new Instinct MI300X AI chip to take on Nvidia’s GPUs
summary: AMD has launched its new Instinct MI300X AI accelerator chip, designed to compete with Nvidia's GPUs in the generative AI market. The company also introduced its Infinity Architecture Platform, powered by eight MI300X chips, and its ROCm software ecosystem. Despite these announcements, AMD's stock fell due to a lack of major customer endorsements for the new chips and details on pricing.

title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison confirms new gen AI service with Cohere during earnings call
summary: Oracle is partnering with Cohere to launch a new generative AI cloud service that will allow enterprises to train customized large language models (LLMs) using their private data while ensuring privacy and security. Oracle founder Larry Ellison announced the collaboration during the company's Q4 earnings call, highlighting Oracle's existing role in AI development and its significant investment in Cohere. This initiative expands Oracle's offerings in the rapidly growing generative AI market, where it competes with other major cloud providers.

title: ETFs Head-to-Head: BetaShares RBTZ' vs Global X ROBO'
summary: This article compares two ASX-listed ETFs focused on AI and robotics: BetaShares Global Robotics and Artificial Intelligence ETF (ASX: RBTZ) and Global X ROBO Global Robotics & Automation ETF (ASX: ROBO). It analyzes their fund objectives, profiles, holdings, performance, and fees, highlighting ROBO's greater diversification and historical outperformance despite higher management costs. The article concludes that while both offer exposure to AI and robotics, ROBO is larger and more diversified.

title: AMD launches new data-center AI chips, software to go up against Nvidia and Intel
summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) unveiled new data-center AI chips and software, including the Instinct MI300X accelerator and MI300A, to compete with Nvidia Corp. and Intel Corp. Despite these announcements at its Data Center & AI Technology Premiere event, AMD's stock declined, finishing down 3.6%. The new products are specifically aimed at handling generative-AI workloads.

title: What will a Vodafone/Three merger mean for 5G in the UK?
summary: A potential merger between Vodafone and Three in the UK is being considered a critical move to ensure their survival and competitive edge in the 5G market, which Three's boss has described as "unsustainable" with current investment spread across four players. The merger, valued at £15bn, would create the UK's largest mobile network operator, challenging existing consolidated players like BT/EE and Virgin Media/O2. However, it faces scrutiny from the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) due to concerns over market share and spectrum holdings, while the UK's 5G rollout continues amidst a ban on Huawei equipment and the increasing integration of AI in network infrastructure.

title: $9B Momentum ETF Is Unrecognizable After Makeover
summary: The iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF (MTUM), valued at $9 billion, has undergone a significant rebalancing, dramatically changing its top holdings and tilting heavily towards technology stocks. This makeover has raised questions about whether the fund is too late to capitalize on the recent tech rally, especially given its recent underperformance compared to the broader market. Despite recent struggles and outflows, MTUM is still a substantial ETF, and its future performance hinges on the durability of current market trends, particularly in technology.

title: Microsoft Inks Deal With NVIDIA-Backed CoreWeave
summary: Microsoft has signed a deal with NVIDIA-backed cloud-computing startup CoreWeave, planning to invest billions to bolster its cloud computing infrastructure for AI operations. This partnership will provide Microsoft easier access to NVIDIA’s GPUs, which are crucial for AI-based applications like ChatGPT, and aims to give Microsoft a competitive edge against rivals like Alphabet Inc. and Amazon Web Services. CoreWeave’s access to over 45,000 GPUs and its status as an elite CSP in the NVIDIA Partner Network positions it as a key enabler for Microsoft's AI endeavors.

title: High Beta ETF 'SPHB' Lifted by Heavy Tech Sector Tilt
summary: The Invesco S&P 500 High Beta ETF (SPHB) performed strongly in May, driven by its significant allocation to the information technology sector. While the broader S&P 500 saw modest gains, the S&P 500 High Beta index climbed 2.4% due to the tech sector's 9.5% rally. SPHB has also demonstrated strong long-term performance, outpacing the S&P 500 over a three-year period.

title: A.I. ETF Sold Out Of Monster Energy, Three Ways To Look At It
summary: The Artificial Intelligence driven ETF (AMOM) unexpectedly sold its entire position in Monster Beverage (MNST), despite Monster's strong performance and growth. The article explores three perspectives on this move, comparing Monster's valuation and performance against Starbucks (SBUX), PepsiCo (PEP), and Coca-Cola (KO), highlighting Monster's aggressive growth trajectory versus the more predictable cash flows and dividends of its peers. The analysis suggests Monster still has significant room for outperformance.

title: CoreWeave Secures $200 Million Series B Extension, Bringing Total Round to $421 Million
summary: CoreWeave, a specialized cloud provider, announced an additional $200 million in Series B funding from Magnetar Capital, bringing its total Series B round to $421 million. This extension comes just one month after their initial $221 million Series B funding, highlighting the accelerated demand for their specialized cloud infrastructure due to the boom in generative AI technology. CoreWeave's focus on GPU-accelerated workloads offers faster and more cost-effective solutions for compute-intensive tasks compared to larger, generalized cloud providers.

title: Serve Robotics to deploy up to 2,000 delivery robots with Uber
summary: Serve Robotics is expanding its partnership with Uber, planning to deploy up to 2,000 delivery robots through Uber Eats across multiple U.S. markets. This collaboration is a significant step towards the mass commercialization of autonomous delivery, building on Serve's successful month-over-month growth since starting operations in 2022. The robots, which started as a division of Postmates (an Uber subsidiary), operate autonomously with advanced sensor technology and can carry substantial loads for long distances on a single charge.

title: NVIDIA Grace Hopper Superchips Designed for Accelerated Generative AI Enter Full Production
summary: NVIDIA announced that its GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip is now in full production, intended to power systems globally for complex AI and HPC workloads. This superchip combines the Arm-based NVIDIA Grace CPU and Hopper GPU architectures using NVLink-C2C interconnect technology, offering significantly higher bandwidth for demanding generative AI applications. Global hyperscalers, supercomputing centers, and numerous system manufacturers are deploying GH200-powered systems, which are expected to be available later this year.

title: NVIDIA Announces DGX GH200 AI Supercomputer
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled the DGX GH200 AI supercomputer, designed to handle massive models for generative AI, recommender systems, and data analytics. This new system connects 256 Grace Hopper Superchips to function as a single 1-exaflop, 144TB GPU, offering significantly more memory than its predecessor. Companies like Google Cloud, Meta, and Microsoft are among the first to explore its capabilities, and NVIDIA is also building its own Helios supercomputer based on this design.

title: Cadence Stock vs Synopsys Stock: The Winner Is?
summary: The article compares Cadence (CDNS) and Synopsys (SNPS), two leading electronic design automation (EDA) software providers, to determine which stock is a better investment. It analyzes their market share, financial performance, valuation, and their use of AI in a mature, well-penetrated market.
